Found it. The domains were never printed; they exist only in the code that computed E(Q) at R 256 (chat "The Method 1.4") and R 465 (chat "The Method 1.6"). Here is what the record holds.

**Domain per item, as computed at R 256 (the thirteen-item table you have):**

| item | domain | blocks · obstacle · cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | physical | one claim · nonexistent · unbounded |
| B | bibliographic | nothing · retrievable · days |
| C | bibliographic | nothing · retrievable · unbounded |
| D | computational | one claim · retrievable · days |
| F | mathematical | nothing · buildable · days |
| G | bibliographic | nothing · retrievable · hours |
| H | physical | one claim · retrievable · days |
| I | physical | one claim · retrievable · days |
| K | mathematical | nothing · retrievable · hours |
| M | computational | one claim · buildable · days |
| N | mathematical | nothing · retrievable · days |
| O | mathematical | one claim · buildable · days |
| P | physical | one claim · retrievable · hours |

Fibre sizes: physical 4, bibliographic 3, mathematical 4, computational 2. `depends` = no on every row.

**The unprinted constraint** (E.4.1's bound, carried in the code as `ok()`): obstacle = buildable ⟹ cost ≤ days. Cells violating it are refused, not counted. Value orders: blocks nothing < novelty < one claim < a result; obstacle retrievable < buildable < nonexistent; cost hours < days < unbounded. Without the constraint and without the fibration you get the inflated figure — that is where your E = 9 comes from.

**Item R — three things you need to know before you finish:**

1. R has no domain on record. It was entered at R 465 (chat "The Method 1.6") and the recomputation there was **unfibred, three coordinates, no domain column**. By the same criterion that placed F, K, N and O, it is mathematical — but that is my placement, not the record's.
2. R was entered as **nothing · buildable · unbounded**. The printed E.1.2 row reads *one claim*. One of the two is wrong and the record does not say which changed or when.
3. The "index predicted it" claim (R 465: unfibred E went 4 → 3 when R entered) was computed **without the E.4.1 constraint**. Under that constraint, buildable · unbounded is a refused cell, not an admitted-and-absent one. So the claim holds only on the unconstrained, unfibred reading. If you want it to survive, either R's obstacle is not buildable or the constraint's status has to be ruled on.

Sources: R 256 computation at claude.ai/chat/5f7147b4-6057…, R 461–465 at claude.ai/chat/3851d6dc-a805…. Nothing above was recomputed in this session; it is read from the transcripts.
